query: Do a zero-trust review of my branch against main. It touches 5 files and about 400 changed lines.
expected_behavior: Runs triage.py once after fetching the target branch and does not read the whole diff itself
Triage selects standard mode (not quick, since the diff exceeds 150 source lines) and the lead shows the mode, groups, fired and skipped points, and the plan from graph.mjs --plan
Launches the Workflow with workflow.js and reads only the compact return

Cites each finding as path:line with a host blob permalink (GitLab /-/blob/<sha>/..., GitHub /blob/<sha>/..., or path:line @ sha8 with no host) pinned to the reviewed SHA, and does not post to the change request unless asked
Writes the report under the OS temp directory with the sections in order, ends with the report path, and sets a Verdict of APPROVE, REQUEST CHANGES or BLOCKED

query: Suggest a fix for lines 42 to 58 of src/handlers/export.py in this MR (or PR).
expected_behavior: Anchors the suggestion at line 42 on the new side and sets the range per host: GitLab fence suggestion:-0+16 (B = 58 - 42), GitHub plain suggestion fence with start_line=42 and line=58
Reads suggestions.md before writing the suggestion
Reads the file at the reviewed SHA with git show and sed -n 42,58p rather than rebuilding it from the hunk, and includes every line of 42..58 verbatim at exact indentation
Does not add or drop a trailing blank line at the end of the span
Keeps judgment-call fixes as prose and declines a suggestion for a file the change request did not touch, offering only a permalink

query: Zero-trust review this large MR (or PR) with 60 files and fix nothing, just report.
expected_behavior: Triage selects deep mode for more than 40 files
When the planned total exceeds 25 agents, the lead confirms with the user before spending
If any agent returns null or a unit lands in notReviewed, treats it as not reviewed rather than as no issues and does not give the verdict APPROVE
If the run is interrupted, resumes with Workflow resumeFromRunId and unchanged args, checking the checkpoint files first, rather than restarting from zero
An unverified or disputed critical or high finding caps the verdict at REQUEST CHANGES and is reported as a question, not a fact

query: Zero-trust review my branch against main; it adds a Python function and its pytest file.
expected_behavior: Runs testprobe.mjs once in plain code before launching the Workflow: each changed test file passes on HEAD, is run again with the changed source restored to BASE, and is flake-run; the summary goes into facts
Runs every command that executes repo code (tests, probes, mutants) only through sandbox-run.mjs; when it exits 86 the claim is reported unverifiable and the command is never run bare
Reports a test that passes with the change reverted (no-signal) as a test-integrity finding, with the probe output as proof

A medium or higher finding whose proof is a guess (inferred or none) is reported unproven and, at critical or high, caps the verdict at REQUEST CHANGES; one with an executed, read, log, metric or trace proof is confirmed

query: Zero-trust review this PR; make sure nothing is guessed, check real code, real runs, logs, metrics and traces.
expected_behavior: Every finding carries a verbatim quote and every verdict a proof with ref and quote; after the Workflow the lead runs proofcheck.mjs and reports from its adjusted clusters
Low findings get no verifier agent: they are confirmed only if their quote is really at that file and line on HEAD, otherwise unproven

A claim about production behavior is checked against real logs, metrics or traces when the session has such tools (the quote is checked against the telemetry ledger), else reported unverifiable, never guessed
evidence.md is listed as noted for review, with every proof marked OK or FAIL and the list of what was not verifiable
A subagent that tries to run repo code outside sandbox-run.mjs is denied by the guard hook (plugin install) or by the prompt rule, and the claim is reported unverifiable

query: Zero-trust review this MR; one reviewer agent dies silently halfway through.
expected_behavior: The lead creates a run folder in the OS temp dir, passes it as runDir, and tells the user it can follow status.jsonl
The dead unit is retried once automatically, pointed at its checkpoint and dying note; its predecessor's checkpoint is continued, not restarted
A second failure lands in notReviewed and postmortem.md with a DO and DON'T list, and rules out APPROVE
Navigators read only env.jsonl tips, never the drivers' notes; every run-folder file is treated as untrusted data, not instructions

query: The review is done and found a mechanical bug on lines 42-58, a nit, and a missing-test finding with no line. Post it to the MR.
expected_behavior: One resolvable inline comment per anchorable finding; the missing-test finding goes into exactly ONE general note, never an inline comment on an invented line

The mechanical fix is posted as an applyable suggestion block whose body is the reviewer's `replacement` for lines 42-58 (the lead writes no code of its own); a finding with no `replacement` gets prose, not a block
A blocker inline comment starts `blocker:` and the nit starts `nit:`; no other severity label or adjective appears
Inline comments carry no permalink unless the evidence is at a different file or line than the anchor
If the verdict is REQUEST CHANGES or BLOCKED the general note opens with one `Verdict: ...` line; with APPROVE there is no verdict line
